title: Mamelodi Sundowns' CAF Champions League Triumph: A Decade of Determination
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Original reporting based on match data, CAF statements and club coverage
summary: After years of heartbreak, Sundowns conquered Africa again, beating AS FAR Rabat 2-1 on aggregate to win the 2025/26 TotalEnergies CAF Champions League.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | May 30, 2026

The journey to continental glory has been long and painful for the Brazilians. After lifting the trophy in 2016 under Pitso Mosimane, Sundowns dominated domestically for almost a decade but kept falling at the final continental hurdle.

Portuguese head coach Miguel Cardoso guided Sundowns to a 1-0 first leg win at Loftus Versfeld and a 1-1 draw in Rabat, sealing a 2-1 aggregate victory over AS FAR. The triumph completes a remarkable season for a club that finished runners-up domestically — just one point behind Orlando Pirates — but ended the campaign as kings of Africa.

title: Orlando Pirates' Historic Treble: How Ouaddou, Appollis and Mofokeng Led the Charge
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Season statistics, club statements and post-match interviews
summary: Orlando Pirates completed a remarkable domestic treble in Abdeslam Ouaddou's debut season, powered by Appollis, Mofokeng and a record-breaking defence.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 1, 2026

The Buccaneers 2025/26 campaign will be remembered as one of the greatest in club history. Moroccan head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou delivered the MTN8, Carling Knockout Cup and the Betway Premiership title — a treble in his very first season, matching the feat last managed by Ruud Krol in 2011.

Pirates finished with a club-record 21 wins from 30 league matches, losing just three times and conceding only 12 goals — the best defence in the division.

title: Bafana Bafana at World Cup 2026: Full Campaign Review
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: FIFA official data, ESPN, Al Jazeera match reports
summary: South Africa made history at World Cup 2026 — reaching the knockout stage for the first time ever. A full review of their incredible campaign.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 29, 2026

What a campaign. Bafana Bafana's return to the World Cup — their first since hosting it in 2010 — ended in the Round of 32, but not before making history by reaching the knockout stage of a World Cup for the very first time.

Group A Results:

  • Mexico 2–0 South Africa (June 11, Azteca) — Quiñones 9', Jiménez 67'. Three red cards.
  • Czechia 1–1 South Africa (June 18, Atlanta) — Sadilek 6' (CZE); Mokoena 83' pen (RSA). A vital point.
  • South Africa 1–0 South Korea (June 24, Monterrey) — Maseko 63'. HISTORY MADE. Bafana qualify.

Round of 32: South Africa 0–1 Canada (June 28, Los Angeles) — Eustaquio 90+2'. Heartbreak at the death.

Teboho Mokoena's cool penalty against Czechia and Thapelo Maseko's stunning 63rd-minute strike against South Korea were the moments that defined the campaign. Khuliso Mudau was outstanding throughout all four games. Hugo Broos, who confirmed his departure after the Canada game, can be proud: "We look back on this World Cup with happiness."

title: Hugo Broos Steps Down: What Next for Bafana Bafana?
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: SAFA statement, post-match press conference
summary: After five years in charge, Hugo Broos has confirmed he is stepping down following Bafana Bafana's historic Round of 32 exit at World Cup 2026.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 29, 2026

Hugo Broos announced his departure after the heartbreaking 0–1 loss to Canada in the Round of 32 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. Stephen Eustaquio's 92nd-minute goal ended what had been a historic World Cup for South Africa.

The Belgian, appointed in 2021, guided Bafana to the 2023 AFCON semi-finals and — most significantly — historic World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002. His squad then went one step further at the tournament itself, beating South Korea to reach the knockout rounds for the first time in the nation's history.

Broos left with a characteristically dignified statement: "We look back on this World Cup with happiness." SAFA is now searching for his replacement, with several local and international names linked to the role.

title: Bafana Bafana Fall to Mexico in Chaotic World Cup Opener
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Match observation, FIFA statistics
summary: South Africa's return to the World Cup ended in a 2-0 defeat to co-hosts Mexico at the Estadio Azteca, in a match that saw three red cards.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 12, 2026

Julián Quiñones gave Mexico an early lead in the 9th minute, and Raúl Jiménez doubled the advantage in the 67th minute. Three red cards were shown — two to South African players and one to Mexico's César Montes in stoppage time.

Despite the numerical disadvantage, South Africa never threatened Mexico's goal. Hugo Broos: "It was a difficult day. We have two more games and must show our character." As it turned out, that character would shine through in the following matches.

title: Mokoena Penalty Earns Bafana Historic Point Against Czechia
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Match observation, FIFA statistics, ESPN
summary: Teboho Mokoena's 83rd-minute penalty cancelled out Michal Sadilek's early opener as South Africa earned a crucial point in Atlanta.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 19, 2026

South Africa showed tremendous character at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta to earn a 1-1 draw against Czechia that kept their World Cup hopes very much alive.

Michal Sadilek gave Czechia the earliest lead of the tournament so far, scoring inside six minutes after linking brilliantly with Sojka. South Africa dominated possession in the second half, creating more chances (xG 1.37 vs 1.02 for Czechia) and were rewarded when referee awarded a penalty after Maseko's shot struck the arm of Sulc in the 81st minute.

Teboho Mokoena stepped up and coolly converted from the spot in the 83rd minute to earn a crucial point. Both sides finished level on 1 point each from two games, setting up a winner-takes-all final matchday.

title: Maseko Stunner Sends Bafana Into History — South Africa 1-0 South Korea
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: FIFA.com, Al Jazeera, ESPN match reports
summary: Thapelo Maseko's brilliant 63rd-minute finish made history as South Africa reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time ever.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 25, 2026 | Source: FIFA.com, Al Jazeera

The scenes at Monterrey Stadium were extraordinary. When Thapelo Maseko collected the ball on the left side of the penalty area in the 63rd minute and curled a clinical left-footed finish into the far corner, South Africa made World Cup history — reaching the knockout rounds of the tournament for the very first time.

South Korea, who had left captain Son Heung-min out of the starting XI in a shock call by coach Myung-Bo Hong, dominated possession (68.4%) but could barely create a chance against a resolute Bafana defence, managing just 1.0 xG compared to South Africa's 1.1.

Hugo Broos' side defended with heart and organisation throughout, soaking up pressure and striking on the counter. When the final whistle blew, the South Africa bench erupted. "For the first time in our history," Broos said afterwards. "This is a great day for South African football." South Africa finished second in Group A with 4 points, setting up a Round of 32 clash with co-hosts Canada in Los Angeles on June 28.

title: Eustaquio 90+2' Breaks Bafana Hearts — SA 0-1 Canada (Round of 32)
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: FIFA.com, ESPN, NBC Sports, Al Jazeera
summary: Canada's Stephen Eustaquio ended South Africa's historic World Cup run with a last-gasp strike at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | June 29, 2026 | Source: FIFA.com, ESPN

After the elation of beating South Korea, Bafana Bafana's extraordinary World Cup came to a heartbreaking end in Los Angeles. Canada's Stephen Eustaquio received the ball on the edge of the South Africa penalty area in the 92nd minute, chested it down, and rifled a perfect finish into the bottom corner past a diving Ronwen Williams.

For 90 minutes South Africa had defended superbly, frustrating a Canada side that had 22 on-target attempts across the group stage. Williams made several excellent saves, and the game seemed destined for extra time. Then came Eustaquio's moment of brilliance.

Canada advance to the Round of 16 to face the Netherlands or Morocco. South Africa exit having made history — reaching the knockouts for the first time ever, winning a World Cup match for the first time, and giving South African football something to build on. Hugo Broos, who confirmed this would be his final match, left the field with his head held high: "We look back on this World Cup with happiness."

title: BREAKING: Mofokeng Signs for Royale Union Saint-Gilloise in R70 Million Deal
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Orlando Pirates official statement, SABC Sport, KickOff.com, Soccer Bullet
summary: Relebohile Mofokeng has completed a blockbuster move to Belgian Pro League side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise on a four-year deal worth over R70 million — flying straight from Los Angeles to Brussels after Bafana's World Cup exit.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | July 3, 2026 | Source: Orlando Pirates statement, SABC Sport, KickOff.com

The move SA football fans had been waiting for is official. Relebohile Mofokeng, 21, has signed a four-year deal with Belgian Pro League club Royale Union Saint-Gilloise, with the transfer fee reported by SABC Sport to be over R70 million. He will wear the No. 38 jersey — the same number he made famous at Orlando Pirates.

In a remarkable touch, Mofokeng did not fly home with his Bafana Bafana teammates after the Round of 32 defeat to Canada in Los Angeles on June 28. Instead, he boarded a flight directly to Brussels to complete his medical and sign personal terms. Orlando Pirates confirmed the deal had actually been agreed before the World Cup, but both clubs deliberately kept it secret to avoid distracting Mofokeng during the tournament.

At his unveiling, Mofokeng said: "I am very happy to be here. It is a dream to play in Europe and to begin our Champions League qualifying campaign soon. The past year has been very special — with the league title, my first FIFA World Cup with South Africa, and now this important step in my career."

The move follows in the footsteps of Percy Tau, who also used Saint-Gilloise as a springboard before moving to Club Brugge, Anderlecht and eventually Brighton in the English Premier League. For South African football, this is another sign of a generation growing in confidence and ambition after the historic World Cup campaign.

Mofokeng made 125 appearances for Pirates, scoring 29 goals and providing 31 assists. Hugo Broos, his biggest advocate, said: "It is a very good move for him. He must do extra work and I will be there — he can call me anytime."

title: Who Should Replace Hugo Broos? Mosimane, Benni McCarthy and Mokwena Lead the Race
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: Times Live, The South African, IOL, EWN, The Citizen — July 10 2026
summary: Hugo Broos has confirmed he is stepping down as Bafana Bafana coach. SAFA now faces the most important appointment in South African football's modern era. We look at the leading candidates.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | July 10, 2026 | Source: Times Live, IOL, EWN, The Citizen

Hugo Broos has confirmed his departure as Bafana Bafana head coach, telling Belgian magazine Humo: "I have already had a conversation with Danny Jordaan. He would like to keep me, but in a different role — as an advisor or something like that. I am returning at the end of July to say my final goodbyes." SAFA officially dismissed reports of his exit on July 10, but the 74-year-old has made clear to Belgian media that his coaching career is over.

Broos leaves as the longest-serving Bafana coach since re-admission in 1992, with a record of 26 wins, 22 draws and 12 losses from 60 matches. His legacy: an AFCON bronze medal in 2024 and, above all, guiding South Africa to the knockout stage of a World Cup for the first time in their history.

So who comes next? Here are the three names dominating the conversation:

1. Pitso Mosimane — The favourite according to most reports. His trophy cabinet is unmatched: multiple PSL titles with Sundowns, the CAF Champions League with both Sundowns and Al Ahly, and a third-place finish at the Club World Cup. The question is whether he would leave club football for the national job.

2. Benni McCarthy — Currently coaching Kenya, the Orlando Pirates and Bafana legend would be a hugely popular appointment with fans. He guided AmaZulu to a historic second-place PSL finish and CAF Champions League qualification. The Sowetan reports he has expressed interest.

3. Rulani Mokwena — The former Mamelodi Sundowns co-coach, who won four consecutive PSL titles, has also reportedly expressed interest. His tactical intelligence is widely respected, and his experience in both the PSL and North Africa (Wydad AC, MC Alger) makes him a credible candidate.

Helman Mkhalele, Broos's longtime assistant, is also in the frame as a continuity option. SAFA must make its decision before the AFCON 2027 qualifiers begin in September 2026.

title: Broos Deserves a Statue — Sports Minister McKenzie Leads Tribute to Departing Coach
author: Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial
source: IOL, SAFA.net, EWN — July 10 2026
summary: Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie says Hugo Broos deserves a statue after leading Bafana Bafana to their best-ever World Cup campaign. We look back at his five-year legacy.
content:
By Matchday Soccer Planet Editorial | July 10, 2026 | Source: IOL, SAFA.net

Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie did not hold back when asked about Hugo Broos. "He deserves a statue," McKenzie said, as tributes poured in for the departing Bafana Bafana coach following South Africa's historic 2026 World Cup campaign.

When Broos arrived in May 2021, Bafana Bafana were ranked outside the top 70 in the world and were the punchline of continental jokes. Five years later, they have reached a World Cup knockout stage for the first time, won bronze at AFCON, and produced a generation of players — Mofokeng, Maseko, Mokoena, Mudau — who are now attracting attention from clubs across Europe.

His methods were simple but effective: select on form, not reputation; build a defensive identity; trust the youth. He once famously dropped veteran players who had been untouchable for years, causing outrage — before being proved right.

Broos is currently in Belgium and plans to return to South Africa at the end of July to say his goodbyes. He has indicated to SAFA president Danny Jordaan that he is open to an advisory role. Ronwen Williams, speaking after the World Cup, summed up the feeling in the camp: "What the coach has done for this country, no one can take away."
